articles.title: TSE julga nova regras para vincular canais de WhatsApp a campanhas eleitorais | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministros discutiram propostas em reunião nesta sexta após impasse sobre canais de apoiadores de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro.
articles.summary: Ministros discutiram propostas em reunião nesta sexta após impasse sobre canais de apoiadores de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro.
articles.body:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) começou a julgar nesta sexta-feira (16) novas regras para definir se um canal em grupo de mensagens instantâneas está ou não vinculado a uma campanha eleitoral.

Pela proposta em análise no plenário virtual da Corte, a associação será a partir de critérios como:

A resolução em debate prevê que o apoio espontâneo não vincula automaticamente um canal a uma campanha.

"O enquadramento do canal como vinculado à campanha demanda a demonstração por elemento objetivamente verificável e submete-se às mesmas regras e disciplina estabelecidas na legislação e nesta resolução, observadas as disposições específicas relativas à natureza do serviço e à forma de divulgação do conteúdo", diz o texto.

A proposta diz ainda que " os responsáveis pelo canal e as respectivas campanhas às quais o respectivo canal estiver vinculado têm o dever de cuidado e de zelar pela licitude dos conteúdos vinculados e higidez das informações e das mensagens veiculadas , vedada a utilização do canal para a transmissão de conteúdo" fabricado ou manipulado para difundir fatos notoriamente inverídicos ou descontextualizados com potencial para causar danos ao equilíbrio do pleito ou à integridade do processo eleitoral.

articles.title: Na TV, Flávio foca em mulheres e Lula associa Flávio a Milei e crise | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PL destacou propostas voltadas à autonomia feminina e mostrou depoimentos de aliadas eleitas, como Caroline de Toni e Bia Kicis. Petista exibiu vídeo de Ivete Sangalo fazendo o “L" e Alckmin disse que o Brasil "não precisa de radicalismos".
articles.summary: Na propaganda eleitoral, Flávio Bolsonaro foca em propostas para mulheres, enquanto Lula critica cortes econômicos do adversário e celebra o fim da escala 6x1.
articles.body:
Na propaganda eleitoral gratuita dos candidatos à Presidência da República desta sexta-feira (16), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) acenou ao eleitorado feminino, detalhando propostas voltadas às mulheres e exibindo o apoio de aliadas. Já Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) criticou as medidas econômicas do candidato do PL e comemorou a aprovação do fim da escala 6x1.

Primeira a ser exibida, a propaganda de Flávio foi dedicada às propostas do "Brasil por Elas", programa do plano de governo registrado na Justiça Eleitoral voltado às mulheres.

O candidato mostrou depoimentos de mulheres demonstrando insatisfação com a economia, inflação e segurança pública no atual governo. "Lula promete, o Brasil sofre", afirmou a campanha.

Entre as propostas, já apresentadas em propagandas anteriores, Flávio destacou medidas de auxílio a crédito para mulheres, rede TEA Brasil e o vale-creche, que propõe vagas em creches particulares caso não haja disponibilidade na rede pública. O presidenciável ainda abordou a redução da maioridade penal e sugeriu que a medida não vai avançar caso Lula seja reeleito.

O programa também exibiu depoimentos de apoio de aliadas políticas do candidato, entre elas Daniella Marques, uma das coordenadoras da campanha.

As senadoras eleitas Caroline de Toni (PL-SC), Bia Kicis (PL-DF) e Gracinha Caiado (União-GO), esposa de Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), candidato à Presidência derrotado no 1º turno, também apareceram na propaganda. O candidato afirmou ter apoio da maioria da bancada feminina eleita no Congresso, caso seja eleito presidente.

Já na propaganda petista, Lula abriu a peça comparando Flávio a Javier Milei, presidente da Argentina, e criticando as medidas econômicas do adversário. O petista sugeriu que a crise deflagrada no país vizinho pode ocorrer no Brasil caso o candidato do PL seja eleito.

"O tesouraço do Flávio Bolsonaro é a motosserra de Milei na Argentina. Quando Flávio Bolsonaro fala em cortes, a despesa que ele quer cortar é você", destacou a propaganda petista.

A peça também voltou a abordar o fim da escala 6x1 no Senado e comemorou a aprovação do projeto no Senado, afirmando ainda que o candidato do PL mudou de posição e acabou votando a favor do projeto por "oportunismo".

Outro trecho da propaganda foi dedicado à mobilização de apoiadores. A peça exibiu um vídeo, viralizado nas redes sociais, da cantora Ivete Sangalo fazendo o “L”.

Na propaganda, o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) defendeu a união de diferentes posições políticas em torno da candidatura. O vice-presidente afirmou que o país "não precisa de radicalismos" e convocou apoiadores a formar uma frente democrática para impedir a volta do bolsonarismo.

Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: REUTERS/Diego Vara e REUTERS/Adriano Machado

articles.title: PF ouve Augusto Lima, ex-sócio de Vorcaro, sobre negócios entre Master e BRB | G1
articles.standfirst: Banqueiro é apontado pelos investigadores como uma das conexões de Vorcaro nas tratativas para que o BRB comprasse carteiras do Banco Master. Depoimento ocorre em Brasília.
articles.summary: Banqueiro é apontado pelos investigadores como uma das conexões de Vorcaro nas tratativas para que o BRB comprasse carteiras do Banco Master. Depoimento ocorre em Brasília.
articles.body:
A Polícia Federal ouve nesta sexta-feira (16) o banqueiro Augusto Ferreira Lima, ex-sócio de Vorcaro, sobre os negócios entre o extinto Banco Master e o Banco de Brasília (BRB).

Augusto Lima prestou depoimento pela manhã e voltou à Superintendência da PF, em Brasília, após o almoço para continuar a oitiva.

O banqueiro é apontado pelos investigadores como uma das conexões de Vorcaro nas tratativas para convencer o BRB a comprar carteiras do Banco Master.

O depoimento de Augusto Lima estava inicialmente marcado para agosto, mas foi adiado a pedido da defesa. À época, a nova data da oitiva ainda não havia sido divulgada.

As investigações têm como base, entre outros elementos, conversas encontradas no celular de Vorcaro.

Augusto Lima foi controlador do Banco Pleno e ex-sócio de Vorcaro. Ele também foi CEO do Banco Master.

Augusto Lima, dono do Banco Pleno — Foto: Vanner Casaes/Agência Alba

O banqueiro foi preso pela Polícia Federal em novembro de 2025, na Operação Compliance Zero. Posteriormente, ele foi solto e passou a usar tornozeleira eletrônica.

A PF já realizou outros depoimentos na investigaçã o que apura supostas irregularidades na proposta de compra do Banco Master pelo BRB. Em janeiro, investigadores ouviram dirigentes e ex-sócios das instituições.

A apuração também envolve a compra, pelo BRB, de carteiras do Banco Master. Segundo as investigações da PF, Augusto Lima atuou para que o banco de Brasília adquirisse essas carteiras.

Em junho, quando foi alvo de uma nova fase da Operação Compliance Zero, a defesa de Augusto Lima afirmou que ele estava à disposição das autoridades para prestar esclarecimentos e disse que os fatos investigados naquela fase eram lícitos.

articles.title: Moraes vota para tornar Oswaldo Eustáquio réu por associação criminosa | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro do STF afirmou que há justa causa para abrir ação penal. Julgamento ocorre no plenário virtual da Primeira Turma e os demais ministros podem votar até 23 de outubro.
articles.summary: Ministro do STF afirmou que há justa causa para abrir ação penal. Julgamento ocorre no plenário virtual da Primeira Turma e os demais ministros podem votar até 23 de outubro.
articles.body:
O ministro Alexandre de Moraes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), votou nesta sexta-feira (16) para tornar réu o blogueiro Oswaldo Eustáquio, apoiador do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, pelo crime de associação criminosa.

Moraes é relator do caso e foi o primeiro a votar no julgamento da Primeira Turma do STF . A análise ocorre no plenário virtual, sistema eletrônico em que os ministros depositam os votos sem uma sessão presencial. Os demais integrantes do colegiado podem votar até 23 de outubro.

Ao votar pelo recebimento da denúncia apresentada pela Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), Moraes afirmou que há justa causa para a abertura de uma ação penal contra Eustáquio.

Se a maioria da Primeira Turma acompanhar o relator, o blogueiro se tornará réu.

A PGR acusa Eustáquio de associação criminosa por sua atuação no período das eleições de 2022 e dos atos antidemocráticos que culminaram nos ataques às sedes dos Três Poderes em 8 de janeiro de 2023.

Segundo a denúncia reproduzida no voto, ele teria usado as redes sociais e participado de manifestações e mobilizações em frente a unidades militares contra o resultado eleitoral , a diplomação e a posse do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

No voto, Moraes afirmou que, nesta etapa do processo, há elementos suficientes para que a denúncia seja recebida.

O ministro ressaltou que o recebimento da acusação não representa uma conclusão definitiva sobre a responsabilidade criminal de Eustáquio.

Segundo ele, nesta fase, basta haver elementos mínimos que indiquem que o crime ocorreu e que o acusado pode ter participado dele.

“Presente a justa causa para a ação penal, a denúncia, portanto, deve ser recebida contra Oswaldo Eustáquio Filho pela prática do crime de associação criminosa”, escreveu Moraes.

O blogueiro bolsonarista Oswaldo Eustáquio, investigado por atos antidemocráticos — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A denúncia da PGR afirma que Oswaldo Eustáquio se associou a outras pessoas e participou de mobilizações que tinham como objetivo praticar atos contra a legitimidade do sistema eleitoral e o Estado Democrático de Direito.

A acusação cita publicações nas redes sociais, manifestações em Brasília e mobilizações em frente a instalações militares.

Segundo a acusação reproduzida no voto, Eustáquio participou, em novembro e dezembro de 2022, de manifestações em Brasília e divulgou mensagens incentivando a adesão aos atos.

Moraes afirmou que a denúncia descreve de forma suficiente as condutas atribuídas ao blogueiro e permite a compreensão da acusação e o exercício do direito de defesa. Para o ministro, não estão presentes motivos para rejeitar a denúncia ou absolver sumariamente Eustáquio nesta fase.

O crime de associação criminosa, previsto no artigo 288 do Código Penal, consiste na associação de três ou mais pessoas com a finalidade específica de cometer crimes. A pena prevista é de um a três anos de prisão.

A defesa de Oswaldo Eustáquio tem afirmado que o julgamento ocorre à revelia e sem respeito ao devido processo legal. Em uma rede social, o blogueiro classificou nesta quinta (15) o julgamento à revelia como “absurdo”.

Em agosto, Alexandre de Moraes determinou que Eustáquio fosse notificado por edital para apresentar resposta à acusação.

Quando a denúncia foi apresentada pela PGR, em agosto, Eustáquio também divulgou uma nota na qual classificou a acusação como “estúpida, patética, inconstitucional”.

Oswaldo Eustáquio participou publicamente de acampamentos que defendiam um golpe de Estado. Segundo a Polícia Federal, ele chegou a se refugiar no Palácio da Alvorada no fim de 2022 por medo de ser preso.

O blogueiro chegou a ser preso no Brasil, passou para a prisão domiciliar e depois deixou o país. Reportagem do g1 publicada em agosto informou que ele fugiu para a Espanha em 2023 e é considerado foragido da Justiça brasileira.

articles.title: Cueva rejeita pedido de Flávio para restringir atuação de sindicatos e estudantes | G1
articles.standfirst: Corregedor do TSE também deu 72 horas para Flávio detalhar as condutas atribuídas a dirigentes citados na ação sobre suposto uso de estruturas de entidades em favor da campanha de Lula.
articles.summary: Corregedor do TSE também deu 72 horas para Flávio detalhar as condutas atribuídas a dirigentes citados na ação sobre suposto uso de estruturas de entidades em favor da campanha de Lula.
articles.body:
O corregedor-geral da Justiça Eleitoral, ministro Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, deu prazo de 72 horas para que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) detalhe as acusações feitas contra dirigentes de sindicatos, entidades estudantis e movimentos sociais em uma ação que aponta suposto uso dessas estruturas em benefício da candidatura à reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Na decisão, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva também negou, por enquanto, uma série de medidas urgentes solicitadas pela campanha de Flávio Nantes Bolsonaro.

Entre as medidas estão pedidos para restringir o uso de estruturas das entidades, impedir repasses de recursos e determinar a preservação de dados e documentos . O pedido de aplicação de multas ficou prejudicado.

Ao analisar a relação de dirigentes apontados na ação, Cueva afirmou que ocupar um cargo de direção não significa, automaticamente, ser responsável por eventual abuso eleitoral cometido por uma entidade.

Segundo a decisão, dos 54 dirigentes apresentados pela campanha, 37 não são citados nominalmente na narrativa dos fatos ou na fundamentação jurídica. Outros sete aparecem somente como signatários de uma nota das centrais sindicais.

A ação foi apresentada por Flávio contra Lula, o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin e dirigentes de centrais sindicais, confederações, federações, sindicatos, entidades estudantis e movimentos sociais.

A campanha acusa os envolvidos de abuso de poder econômico e político e de uso indevido dos meios de comunicação social.

O recebimento da ação, porém, não significa que o tribunal tenha considerado verdadeiras as acusações ou reconhecido a existência de irregularidades.

O próprio ministro ressalvou na decisão que essas questões ainda dependerão da produção de provas.

Lula e Flávio disputam o segundo turno da eleição presidencial, marcado para 25 de outubro.

Ministro Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, corregedor-geral da Justiça Eleitoral — Foto: Luiz Roberto/TSE

O corregedor-geral determinou que a campanha de Flávio informe, individualmente, quais fatos atribui a cada um dos demais dirigentes citados na ação.

Para cada pessoa, a campanha terá de apontar o fato atribuído, a respectiva data, a prova correspondente e explicar de que forma o ato teria contribuído para o abuso alegado.

Se isso não for feito no prazo de 72 horas, a ação poderá ser rejeitada em relação aos dirigentes cujas condutas não forem individualizadas.

Até uma nova decisão, esses dirigentes não deverão ser notificados para apresentar defesa, mesmo que seus nomes já apareçam no cadastro do processo.

O ministro decidiu, entretanto, receber a ação contra Lula e Alckmin e cinco dirigentes para os quais considerou haver condutas delimitadas na petição.

Eles terão cinco dias para apresentar defesa.

Cueva rejeita proibição ampla contra entidades

Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva negou o pedido da campanha de Flávio Nantes Bolsonaro para que dirigentes fossem proibidos, até 25 de outubro, de utilizar sedes, empregados, veículos, recursos financeiros, sites, perfis institucionais, jornais, canais de mensagens e cadastros de filiados das entidades para propaganda favorável a Lula e Alckmin, ou contrária ao candidato do PL.

Segundo o corregedor, a solicitação resultaria em uma ordem genérica sobre manifestações futuras e ainda desconhecidas.

O ministro afirmou que é preciso analisar individualmente o conteúdo, as circunstâncias e os meios utilizados para definir se uma manifestação configura propaganda eleitoral irregular.

Na avaliação do ministro, uma restrição nos termos pedidos poderia ter efeito inibidor indevido sobre as liberdades de expressão, associação e organização sindical e se aproximar de censura prévia.

Ao mesmo tempo, ele ressaltou que a negativa não autoriza propaganda irregular nem impede a investigação de eventual uso abusivo das estruturas institucionais.

Pedido envolvendo entidades estudantis também é rejeitado

O corregedor também negou a ordem solicitada contra a União Nacional dos Estudantes (UNE). A campanha queria obrigar a entidade a orientar organizações estudantis vinculadas a ela a não utilizar centros acadêmicos e outros espaços de instituições públicas de ensino para armazenar ou distribuir material eleitoral.

Para Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, não foram apresentados elementos suficientes que demonstrassem o uso efetivo desses espaços para essa finalidade, nem houve individualização dos locais e das atividades que justificariam a intervenção da Justiça.

A decisão também cita a proteção constitucional às manifestações políticas no ambiente universitário.

Outro pedido negado, por ora, determinaria que Meta, X e Google, responsável pelo YouTube, preservassem dados, registros, métricas e conteúdos relacionados às publicações citadas na ação, inclusive material eventualmente apagado.

As entidades também seriam obrigadas a conservar documentos fiscais, contratos, atas e outros registros relacionados aos episódios descritos pela campanha.

O corregedor considerou que o pedido não delimitou suficientemente quais dados e documentos deveriam ser preservados, quem seria responsável por guardá-los, os períodos abrangidos e a relação de cada elemento com os fatos investigados.

A negativa, segundo a decisão, não impede uma nova análise caso seja apresentado um requerimento mais específico.

A campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro também pediu uma ordem para impedir entidades sindicais, com exceções previstas na própria ação, de repassar dinheiro, bens ou serviços estimáveis em dinheiro a comitês, frentes, brigadas ou outras estruturas favoráveis a candidaturas.

Cueva rejeitou o pedido neste momento. Na decisão, diferenciou manifestação política de eventual contribuição econômica eleitoral e afirmou que é necessário examinar as circunstâncias concretas de cada iniciativa. Também considerou abrangente demais a ordem solicitada.

O ministro ressaltou, contudo, que a decisão não libera o uso de recursos sindicais de forma contrária à legislação eleitoral.

A campanha ainda havia solicitado multa de R$ 50 mil por ato ou publicação em descumprimento pelos investigados e de R$ 100 mil por hora de descumprimento pelos provedores.

Como as medidas de urgência correspondentes foram rejeitadas, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva considerou prejudicado o pedido de multas, por não haver, neste momento, obrigação judicial a ser assegurada pelas penalidades.

Um ponto, porém, ficou pendente de decisão: o pedido para desativar um chamado “Comitê de Apoio à reeleição do Presidente Lula”, que, segundo a ação, teria sido instalado na sede do Sindicato dos Trabalhadores dos Correios do Rio de Janeiro (SINTECT-RJ).

O ministro deu 24 horas para que o sindicato explique em que consiste o comitê, se houve disponibilização de estrutura física e de recursos da entidade e se ele continua funcionando. Só depois desses esclarecimentos ou do fim do prazo o ministro analisará o pedido de desativação.

Corregedor do TSE afirmou que ocupar cargo de direção não basta para responsabilizar alguém por eventual abuso eleitoral; ministro também rejeitou, por ora, ordens abrangentes contra sindicatos e entidades estudantis.

articles.title: Datafolha mostra desafios de candidatos: Flávio Bolsonaro tem de evitar mais perda de votos; Lula precisa ganhar eleitores | G1
articles.body:
Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) durante propaganda eleitoral gratuita na quarta-feira (14). — Foto: Reprodução

O resultado da pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira (15) trouxe desafios para os dois candidatos. Empatados tecnicamente, mas com Flávio Bolsonaro numericamente à frente, (47% a 45%), o levantamento traz alertas para o candidato do PL e para o presidente Lula .

Flávio Bolsonaro oscilou para baixo dois pontos percentuais , resultado da campanha disseminada pelo PT do medo da volta dos Bolsonaro feita pela campanha petista, recuando de 49% para 47% na comparação com a última pesquisa.

Já o presidente Lula precisa conquistar intenções de voto, o que ele não conseguiu até agora. Entre uma pesquisa e outra, ficou estacionado nos 45% . A vantagem do filho do ex-presidente Bolsonaro é que as intenções de voto perdidas não foram para o petista, mas para indecisos, brancos e nulos.

Eleitores que declararam intenção de anular o voto ou votar em branco subiram de 5% para 6%, e indecisos variaram de 1% para 2%. Isso mostra que um eleitorado que declarou intenção de votar no filho do ex-presidente após o primeiro turno agora está indeciso ou pode não votar.

Lula estável nos 45% mostra que as manifestações de rua animaram a militância petista, mas ainda não aumentaram os votos de Lula . Em votos válidos, Flávio Bolsonaro recuou de 52% para 51%, enquanto Lula foi de 48% para 49% na comparação das duas últimas pesquisas.

O resultado da pesquisa foi bem-recebido pela campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro. Segundo eles, o candidato do PL manteve grande vantagem no Sudeste, Sul e Centro-Oeste. Na avaliação de interlocutores do senador do PL, manter a vantagem no Sudeste é crucial para ganhar a campanha.

A equipe de Lula comemorou a pesquisa. A avaliação é que Lula conteve o crescimento de Flávio Bolsonaro e que há possibilidades de ele começar a crescer exatamente a partir deste fim de semana.

articles.title: Meta nega interferência política nas eleições do Brasil e cita 'incidentes  técnicos' em redes de Lula  | G1
articles.standfirst: Na quinta-feira (15), o ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze, do TSE, determinou, que até o fim do segundo turno das eleições, a Meta não interfira na distribuição de conteúdo político nem de Lula (PT) nem de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
articles.summary: Na quinta-feira (15), o ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze, do TSE, determinou, que até o fim do segundo turno das eleições, a Meta não interfira na distribuição de conteúdo político nem de Lula (PT) nem de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
articles.body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

A Meta, responsável pelo Facebook, Instagram e Whatsapp, disse nesta sexta-feira (16), em nota, que a empresa "não toma partido nessa nem em nenhuma outra eleição", afirmou que a conta do presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) chegou a ser suspensa "por engano" e que "incidentes técnicos recentes" afetaram as duas campanhas na internet.

De acordo com o posicionamento, uma "lacuna" nas "proteções" da empresa fez com que a ferramenta de inteligência artificial da Meta elaborasse materiais de campanha que favoreciam o senador e também candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

"Nossos sistemas não classificam nem distribuem conteúdo com base em ideologia política, e nossas regras e sua aplicação valem igualmente para todos", declarou a empresa na nota.

A decisão foi dada em ação protocolada pela campanha de Lula, após dizer que a empresa "tem falhado, de forma reiterada e sistemática, na entrega de postagens da coligação".

De acordo com a Meta, a conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula (PT) foi desativada "por engano" e "não por razões políticas" em 23 de setembro . A suspensão, segundo a empresa, durou pouco mais de 1 hora - e a página oficial da campanha de Lula no Facebook e a conta no Instagram nunca foram bloqueadas.

"Em 23 de setembro, a conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula foi desativada por engano por pouco mais de uma hora, após um anúncio ter sido classificado como uma possível tentativa de se passar por um programa social do governo durante uma análise mais ampla de combate a fraudes. A análise antifraude incorreta feita sobre este anúncio foi adotada no âmbito de um acordo firmado em 13 de abril de 2026 com a Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) para combater golpes envolvendo programas federais".

A empresa afirmou que suspensão ocorreu por conta "das regras rígidas do Brasil para conteúdo digital" que, na avaliação da Meta, "aumentam o risco de aplicação excessiva e ameaçam a liberdade de expressão".

"Desde 2025, essas regras ampliaram a possível responsabilidade das plataformas por conteúdo e anúncios gerados por terceiros".

Em 7 de outubro , a empresa disse que "um incidente técnico" afetou os sistemas que contabilizam reproduções e reprises de Reels. O problema, ainda segundo a Meta, não ficou ficou restrito ao Brasil e à conta da campanha de Lula. "É importante destacar que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro também entrou em contato com a Meta neste dia para relatar o mesmo problema".

"Durante cerca de cinco horas, as contagens de visualizações ficaram congeladas, incorretas ou zeradas, embora o conteúdo continuasse sendo distribuído normalmente. O incidente afetou criadores em mais de 100 países."

A empresa reportou ainda que, em 9 de outubro , a Meta identificou uma falha global no Gerenciador de Anúncios, causada por uma atualização de código, que impediu temporariamente anunciantes de criar anúncios a partir de publicações já feitas no Instagram.

Usuários da Meta AI no WhatsApp relatam que a tecnologia se recusa a gerar imagens de campanha de Lula, mas aceita pedidos semelhantes para o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro. "O incidente envolvendo a Meta AI em 14 de outubro resultou de uma lacuna específica em nossas proteções, e não de viés político".

🔎 A Meta AI é um assistente de inteligência artificial gratuito e integrado ao WhatsApp, Instagram e Facebook. Ela funciona de forma semelhante ao ChatGPT nos serviços da Meta e, a partir de descrições simples, pode produzir textos, planejar atividades e criar imagens, por exemplo.

O posicionamento divulgado pela empresa afirmou que, para cumprir as regras eleitorais, a Meta proibiu temporariamente a Meta AI de recomendar candidatos ou gerar imagens deles no Brasil.

"Nossos sistemas bloqueavam prompts no Brasil que mencionavam claramente qualquer um dos candidatos – incluindo “Lula”, “Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva”, “Bolsonaro” e “Flávio Bolsonaro” -, mas nem sempre reconheciam um candidato quando um primeiro nome comum era combinado com um número eleitoral".

A empresa declarou também que "cada um dos incidentes citados pela campanha de Lula tem uma explicação direta e documentada".

"Nenhum deles reflete direcionamento político. Nenhum reflete manipulação da distribuição. Nenhum reflete uma tentativa de influenciar a eleição", conclui.

articles.title: Power struggle erupts in Trump's White House as midterm losses loom
articles.summary: White House aides, who have kept clashes muted during President Donald Trump's second term, have begun jostling more openly for power as they brace for wides...
articles.body:
White House aides, who have kept clashes muted during President Donald Trump's second term, have begun jostling more openly for power as they brace for widespread midterm election losses and internal upheaval, according to interviews with 20 staffers, advisers and people close to the president.

The interviews, most of which were conducted on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel machinations, paint a picture of infighting that has started to resemble the pitched battles of Trump's first term.

Believing that Chief of Staff Susie Wiles might step down after the election, a handful of Trump aides, including Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, top housing official Bill Pulte and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin, have begun angling for the position should it become available.

Wiles has given no indication to aides or allies that she plans to leave. Still, high-level White House staffers frequently cycle out of their stressful jobs after 18 months to two years, and Trump had four chiefs of staff, including an acting one, during his first term.

The past week in the White House has been "the new Wild Wild West," one Trump ally said.

The jockeying started in earnest last week after Trump first reached out to Katie Zacharia about joining the administration as the new White House press secretary, a move he made without consulting Wiles, according to four people familiar with the decision. The unilateral action by the president was viewed internally as undermining Wiles, creating the impression of a less-disciplined operation and an unsettled center of power inside the West Wing.

For longtime observers of Trump's inner circle, the friction this week harks back to his first term, when shifting factions of aides and family members vied for power and undermined one another in the process - a pattern this White House has mostly avoided, until now.

Compounding the uncertainty is the president, who has told allies he feels frustrated that no one is publicly defending him as vociferously as he would like 18 days before the midterm elections. Trump has embarked on a frenzied schedule of campaign rallies in the final stretch to juice enthusiasm among the Republican faithful, but with a historically low approval rating and growing voter frustration about high prices, he and the Republican Party face major political headwinds.

The president has been calling friends, White House aides and outside advisers because he appears worried that information is not reaching him, according to an adviser who received one of the calls. In these conversations, he has also vented about the midterms and the two outside advisers quarterbacking his political strategy, James Blair and Chris LaCivita, who are close allies of Wiles.

Among those who have been in contact with Trump is former aide Corey Lewandowski, a fierce rival of Wiles's, who is supportive of Pulte, according to two people with knowledge of the conversations.

Reached for comment, Lewandowski said: "I have never spoken with the president about Bill Pulte being the chief of staff."

"These anonymous sources know nothing. It's the same selfish, opportunistic behavior from people more focused on themselves than on President Trump, whose priority is delivering for the American people and winning the midterms," Danielle Alvarez, a White House spokesperson, said in response to a request for comment. "President Trump has assembled a strong, talented and united team focused on his America First agenda - not the egos and political games of anonymous outsiders."

Internal GOP polling shows that support for Republican candidates cratered after the party's midterm convention in Dallas, with voters saying the party was not attuned to their economic concerns, according to a Republican strategist briefed on the numbers. Rather than campaigning extensively in September, Trump spent much of the month hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House and working on his construction projects, including a new White House helipad and his proposed ballroom.

Although the White House continues to express confidence in public, many Trump aides and allies believe they will lose control of the House of Representatives, although by how large a margin remains unclear. Trump advisers and Republican strategists say the fate of the Senate is a 50-50 proposition, despite a deluge of spending in recent weeks by the president's main super PAC, MAGA Inc., and the Senate Leadership Fund. They acknowledge that typically red states, including Kansas and Texas, are in play.

Whether Wiles will opt to stay in her position if the midterms yield major GOP losses has emerged as a dominant topic in Trumpworld.

A Republican "blowout next month, very likely, will be a wedge that the ambitious use" to slide into the chief of staff's office, one Wiles ally said.

The jockeying to become the next chief of staff has taken various forms. Pulte frequently lugs poster boards onto the golf course, Marine One or Air Force One to try to nudge Trump to sign on to his ideas.

Typically, the poster boards contain Pulte's proposals to handle whatever issue is irking the president that day - be it the renovations to the Kennedy Center or the Federal Reserve's failure to lower interest rates. Sometimes the posters include artwork of the president, or images of his rallies, according to one person who has viewed the posters. Trump's love of visual aids has its limits; he has told advisers that Pulte has brought him so many poster boards that they are cluttering up the White House residence, said two White House officials and a third person close to the White House.

Wiles ran Trump's highly disciplined 2024 presidential campaign and paved the way for him and his team to take swift action through more than 100 executive orders during his first 100 days in office. While she does not consider herself a policy expert, she has inserted herself into the center of the administration's debates on global tariffs and potential guardrails for artificial intelligence, as both became political liabilities for the president.

But Wiles and her inner circle were put on the defensive recently after Blair and LaCivita traveled to Republika Srpska - the Serbian-dominated portion of Bosnia - to do political consulting work for the pro-Russian government.

That created problems for Wiles, who had brought both men into Trump's 2024 campaign. The president has always bristled when current or former aides profit off their connections to him.

Trump responded by posting a pointed message on Truth Social distancing himself from Blair and LaCivita and promising to fire them if their consulting work posed a conflict of interest.

The story got worse for the chief of staff when a photo surfaced of her daughter, Katie Wiles, on a visit to Republika Srpska. The younger Wiles is a partner at the lobbying firm Continental Strategy, which represents the territory's government (though she is not individually named on the firm's lobbying disclosure forms). Detractors of Wiles, LaCivita and Blair have been fueling the tensions and stoking Trump's suspicions by showing him critical articles about the foreign consulting, three outside advisers said.

Blair and LaCivita are still leading Trump's midterm strategy, and the president still talks to Blair frequently, but his initial unhappiness with their trip may have weakened the duo's ability to offer guidance and issue directives to various campaigns, one Republican strategist said.

articles.title: A growing number of prominent Republicans are endorsing Democrats in 2026
articles.summary: In 2010, Ken Buck rode the tea party wave to win Colorado’s Republican Senate nomination but proved too conservative for the state’s general-election voters.
articles.body:
In 2010, Ken Buck rode the tea party wave to win Colorado's Republican Senate nomination but proved too conservative for the state's general-election voters.

In 2022, Don Bolduc rode a similar arc in the New Hampshire Senate race as an election-denier who spouted a conspiracy theory about Bill Gates and vaccines .

This week, both Buck and Bolduc endorsed Democrats for major statewide offices in their respective states. Buck backed Democratic state Attorney General Phil Weiser for Colorado governor, while Bolduc backed Rep. Chris Pappas for Senate in New Hampshire.

And they're part of a growing list of Republicans making similar crossover endorsements.

Sometimes the endorsements are about opposing the GOP's Trump-era exploits. But other times, they appear somewhat personal.

The impact of any of these endorsements could be limited. As the 2024 Democratic presidential nominee, Kamala Harris touted the support of Republicans including former Vice President Dick Cheney, former Rep. Liz Cheney and former Sen. Jeff Flake, among other Republicans, and she still lost. But they're notable all the same.

Buck's endorsement of Weiser is a little less surprising, given the former congressman drifted away from his party late in his House tenure in 2023 and 2024. Weiser's GOP opponent, Victor Marx, is also a highly unorthodox candidate who recently spoke openly about slamming his wife against a door . (His wife says it was not domestic abuse and that it was self-defense practice.)

Bolduc's move will raise more eyebrows. The retired Army brigadier general is endorsing against a standard-issue Republican nominee in former Sen. John E. Sununu. But Sununu's brother, then-Gov. Chris Sununu, endorsed Bolduc's opponent in the 2022 primary and called Bolduc " not a serious candidate ."

Other prominent Republicans have also endorsed key Democratic candidates in 2026.

In Kansas, two former governors — Mike Hayden and Bill Graves — are backing Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton over GOP Sen. Roger Marshall. Both criticized Marshall's decision to go along with Trump policies that they argue are bad for Kansas and the country.

Flake, the former Arizona senator, has backed Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff for reelection in Georgia over MAGA GOP Rep. Mike Collins.

Two former chairmen of the Republican National Committee have also endorsed Democratic congressional candidates in their states. Former Montana Gov. Marc Racicot is backing union leader and former smokejumper Sam Forstag in the 1st District. And in Florida, former Sen. Mel Martinez announced Thursday that he's backing former NASA chief of staff Bale Dalton in that state's 7th District.

(Racicot, like Flake, has backed prominent Democrats before.)

In Illinois, former GOP state House leader Jim Durkin is backing Democratic Gov. J.B. Pritzker for reelection over Republican nominee Darren Bailey, with whom Durkin has clashed before .

Republican South Dakota Secretary of State Monae Johnson is endorsing the Democrat running for her job after losing at her party's convention. Johnson's evolution is also interesting ; she had in her 2022 campaign declined to say whether then-President Joe Biden had legitimately defeated Trump in 2020 and ran on "election integrity" like many election-deniers were at the time.

In the high-profile Texas Senate race, a number of well-known Republicans are backing Democratic state Rep. James Talarico against state Attorney General Ken Paxton, whose personal baggage has alienated many conservatives in the state.

And in perhaps the most shocking crossover endorsement, former George W. Bush strategist Karl Rove said he would back Democrat Jon Rosenthal for Texas railroad commissioner over Republican Bo French. That came after French posted an image of brown-skinned students at a University of Texas football game and complained about the replacement of Americans by foreigners.

Rove said he had only voted for one other Democrat — all the way back in 1994.

Crossover endorsements have gone the other way, too, with some well-known moderate Democrats, or former Democrats, backing Republicans in key races.

Retiring Maine Rep. Jared Golden recently announced he would back New York GOP Rep. Mike Lawler for reelection. Former Sen. Joe Manchin of West Virginia, who became an independent before retiring from the Senate, backed GOP Sen. Susan Collins of Maine and Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania. And former Sen. Kyrsten Sinema of Arizona, who also became an independent, is supporting GOP congressional candidate Jay Feely in her state, Axios reported .

But the GOP crossovers for Democrats are more numerous — and come from more interesting places.

articles.title: Ilhan Omar's sister skips book tour event amid week of chaos following raid on progressive's DC home
articles.summary: Sahra Noor skipped a scheduled book tour event in Rochester, Minnesota, after reportedly being subpoenaed in the Ilhan Omar immigration fraud probe.
articles.body: ROCHESTER, Minn. — The older sister of embattled Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., who is currently on a book tour promoting a memoir about her life as a Somali immigrant, skipped a scheduled event due to a "family emergency" amid the fallout from the raid on the congresswoman's home. As Omar faces a federal government probe related to potential immigration fraud as well as a separate investigation into her financial disclosures, Sahra Noor was scheduled for a book tour stop at the University of Minnesota Rochester on Thursday night. Noor, who came to the United States as a refugee alongside Omar and other family members in the 1990s, was reportedly subpoenaed in relation to the immigration investigation into her sister. She currently lives in Nairobi, Kenya, according to her LinkedIn page, but is on a worldwide book tour promoting her recently-released "Salt in the Snow: A Somali Immigrant Story." ILHAN OMAR’S HUSBAND INSISTS HE HAS ‘NO CONCERNS’ AMID FEDERAL IMMIGRATION INVESTIGATION Fox News Digital reached out to Noor for comment but did not hear back at time of publication. According to a flyer, which was posted on Facebook by Rochester-based bookstore Garden Party Books, the event was scheduled for Thursday night at 6:30 p.m. It was set to be held at the Intercultural Student Center at the University of Minnesota Rochester. When Fox News Digital arrived for the event, the space was completely empty. Fox News Digital had previously RSVP'd for the event via a QR code on the flyer and did not receive any communication that the event had been canceled, rescheduled or relocated. Garden Party Books told Fox News Digital the event was canceled due to a Noor "family emergency." Noor's absence from the book tour stop comes amid rumors that Omar fled the United States following the raid earlier this week. While the congresswoman has not been seen in public since Monday's raid, her husband snapped when asked outside the home on Wednesday whether he had a response to the rumors that she fled the country. The flyer said that Garden Party Books, along with the University of Minnesota Bookstores and the Rochester Public Library, were "proud supporters" of the event. It also described Noor as a "poet, storyteller and health system leader," and said the book is a "story of migration, motherhood, grief and family." According to Noor's website, her book was officially launched during an event in a Nairobi bookstore on Aug. 13, 2026. She appeared in early September at a festival in Cape Town, South Africa to promote her work. OMAR RAID DRAWS OMINOUS WARNING FROM VANCE AS HE BLASTS PROGRESSIVE REP'S 'RAGE' TOWARD AMERICA Now, she is touring in the United States. Noor held an Oct. 1 event in Minneapolis, and another five days later at the University of Minnesota. She hosted an event in St. Paul, Minnesota on Oct. 7. Her next scheduled event is at the Somali Community Cultural Innovation Hub in Seattle on Oct. 23. Federal agents with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the leading investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), executed a search warrant on Omar's home starting at around 6:00 a.m. on Monday morning. ILHAN OMAR'S HUSBAND SNAPS OVER RUMORS SHE FLED US AFTER FEDERAL IMMIGRATION FRAUD RAID Fox News Digital first reported Monday that the raid stems from an investigation into whether Omar or her late father, Nur Mohamed, fraudulently filled out her citizenship paperwork decades ago. The investigation, two sources noted, could lead to the congresswoman's denaturalization. The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Omar's phone, passport and computers were seized in the raid. Omar has described the search as an "outrageous abuse of power" and called it an "unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies." articles.title: Black civic group blasts Talarico campaign over canceled event: ‘Deeply disappointed’
articles.summary: James Talarico faces frustration from Black voter groups over a canceled event and questions about whether his $25 million outreach pledge is real.
articles.body: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico is facing lingering frustration from inside his own political backyard over the cancellation of an event that was supposed to take place on Oct. 5 with a Black civic-service group. The Central Texas African American Civic Engagement Symposium (CT-AACES) expressed deep frustration in an email, sent to the Talarico campaign and obtained by Fox News Digital, after the campaign cancelled an event – which had 325 confirmed registrants – during Talarico's two-week absence from the campaign trail due to illness. CT-AACES said the cancellation left them with "irrecoverable financial loss," and that Talarico's campaign had not engaged in rescheduling efforts "While we understand Representative Talarico’s health required priority, we are deeply disappointed by the campaign’s decision to issue a flat cancellation rather than committing to a rescheduled date," the email reads. "It was a missed opportunity for Representative Talarico to directly address community skepticism and demonstrate the sincerity of his commitment to Central Texas African Americans." The cancellation is the most recent instance of the tensions that Talarico's campaign has faced with the Black community. It also casts doubt on the effectiveness of his efforts to reach Black voteBlack voters through a $25 million outreach pledge aimed at mobilizing black voters is fully reaching the ground. TALARICO DISAPPEARANCE HAS DEM VOLUNTEERS WORRYING AND TRUMP ASKING, 'WHAT IS GOING ON?' The frustration isn’t isolated to CT-AACES. At least one Austin-area Democratic operative who has met directly with Talarico told Fox News Digital that she remains frustrated by what she described as uneven follow-through on outreach to Black Democrats and candidates further down the ballot. "Black voters aren't a monolith," the source cautioned, rejecting any blanket assertion that Black Texans distrust Talarico outright. "I think that there are pockets that do. There's a pocket that doesn’t. And then there's the pocket that's really unsure," she said. The operative, who previously ran for Talarico's prior state House seat and spoke to Fox News Digital, is particularly familiar with the nominee and the Democratic organizing landscape in the Austin region. Asked about a $25 million investment to focus on door-knocking in Black neighborhoods, in-person community events and engagement with Black churches, the source said those investments haven’t manifested yet. "We haven't received the money, but we're being told it's coming," she said of some accounts she has heard from the ground. "We received, you know, one or 2% of what we were told we were going to get. And then it's been silence since," she said. DAVID MARCUS: HOW CROCKETT'S LAST STAND IN TEXAS COULD BRING DOWN TALARICO The comments come after Talarico appeared on a Black voter coalition Zoom last week, delivering brief remarks about "put[ting] in the money … time … and effort to win" before his feed disappeared from the call reportedly without a public question-and-answer session. At the July Houston town hall where Talarico announced the $25 million pledge, nurse Kandice Webber confronted him as the event approached its scheduled end and demanded that he remain to answer questions. "Black people don’t trust you for this reason," she said, according to the Texas Tribune . "And you cannot win without us, so you stay here and you answer our questions, or you suffer the consequences," Webber said. During his primary, Talarico also encountered controversy over the black vote when reports surfaced the he had characterized rival candidate and former NFL linebacker Collin Allred as a "mediocre Black man." "He had the audacity to say to a Black woman that he had signed up to run against a mediocre black man," Allred said in a video response posted to X. "We should say ‘thank you.’ Thank you for taking off the mask. Thank you for telling us who you really are and what you really think… keep my name out of your mouth while you’re at it." Talarico, for his part, described the wording as a mischaracterization, stating that he "described Congressman Allred’s method of campaigning as mediocre" and that he would "never attack him on the basis of race." Talarico also received criticism from Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, his primary opponent in the Senate primary, after she accused him of darkening her skin in campaign ads against her. "And you know, I've been asked a couple of times about it. And you know, I look at this specifically as a civil rights lawyer, and I see when they're sending out ads and they're darkening my skin. And I'm just like, I know what this is, right?" Crockett said at a press conference. The operative said she personally pressed Talarico during a June meeting to do more to endorse and support down-ballot Democrats after hearing from campaigns that donors had already exhausted their political giving on his Senate bid and were asking whether he had endorsed those candidates. FOX NEWS POLL: IT’S A LONE STAR SENATE SHOWDOWN BETWEEN TALARICO AND PAXTON "He was very gracious. He said he understood," she told Fox News Digital. "I followed up with his staff multiple times and to this day have still not heard anything, which has been really frustrating to me." articles.title: Dimite Montse Mínguez, portavoz del PSOE, tras las críticas de la oposición hacia su pareja por sus negocios inmobiliarios
articles.standfirst: La decisión la comunicó en sus redes sociales y afirmó que se va con la conciencia “tranquila” y la cabeza “alta”
articles.summary: La decisión la comunicó en sus redes sociales y afirmó que se va con la conciencia “tranquila” y la cabeza “alta”
articles.body: Montse Mínguez, portavoz del PSOE, anunció este viernes, 16 de octubre, su dimisión a través de un mensaje en redes sociales. Esto provoca que dé un paso al lado en lo que respecta a la formación que lidera Sánchez y, también, que salga de las listas de cara a las próximas elecciones generales del domingo, 29 de noviembre. Montse Mínguez tomó esta decisión tras las críticas de la oposición a los negocios inmobiliarios de pareja, Sergi Vélez Viola, empresario vinculado al mencionado sector. PP y Vox criticaron que sus negocios fueran en contra de las políticas del PSOE para facilitar el acceso a la vivienda. Y es que, según indicaron dichas formaciones, gestionaba unos 30 inmuebles, con sociedades vinculadas a su actividad empresarial en Panamá. El partido que lidera Abascal pidió explicaciones por una subvención pública de 200.000 euros concedida a una empresa relacionada con él. Todo ello, derivó en el adiós de Mínguez que comunicó su postura de la siguiente forma en un mensaje difundido en redes sociales: “He tomado la decisión de dar un paso atrás, convencida de que es lo mejor para el proyecto colectivo al que le he dedicado mi esfuerzo, mi compromiso y mis mejores energías”. “Vivimos un momento decisivo. Un momento crucial para nuestro país y los valores que defendemos. Cuando la ultraderecha llama a las puertas y pretende cuestionar avances sociales, derechos y consensos que han costado años construir, nuestra responsabilidad debe estar por encima de cualquier consideración personal”, siguió diciendo. Por último, la ya exportavoz del PSOE quiso agradecer la confianza, el apoyo y el afecto que recibió “durante este tipo” y afirmó que se va con la conciencia “tranquila”, con la cabeza “alta” y la fidelidad “intacta a sus principios”.

articles.title: Trump's new press secretary out of the job just days after rocky debut
articles.summary: Katie Zacharia has been fired as White House Press Secretary.
articles.body: Katie Zacharia is leaving her role as White House press secretary after only seven days following a rocky first week on the job, a source familiar confirmed to Fox News Digital. President Donald Trump told Zacharia to "reconsider" the role, revealing to members of the press on the South Lawn on Friday that he told her: "You don't have to do this if you don't want to… I think you should reconsider." A senior White House official tells Fox News that Katie is now "transitioning out" of the role. It comes as her one-week tenure was marked by mounting scrutiny over her legal credentials and a rocky debut before the White House press corps on Tuesday. Critics have taken aim at Zacharia over her recent interviews attempting to recover from the bumpy start. Zacharia was named to the role Oct. 9 and stepped behind the White House podium for her first press briefing just days later on Oct. 13. The briefing lasted 14 minutes and Zacharia took only three questions. "Maybe it’s not for her," Trump acknowledged in his brief remarks outside the White House on Friday. TRUMP NAMES LEAVITT SUCCESSOR AFTER WEEKS OF SPECULATION — AND SHE'S NO STRANGER TO MAGA When pressed if this update meant that Trump fired Zacharia, the president walked back. "No no. I want her to have a good life," he said. "She’s been brutalized by the media," Trump added. During an appearance on "Hannity" Thursday night, Zacharia was pressed over whether she could refer to herself as an attorney. Zacharia admitted she did not pass the bar exam and never obtained a law license in the United States. "I had already pre-registered for the bar exam, and basically during the summer, I knew I would be living in China and the result of the bar would be inconsequential. I sat for it because I didn't want to have a withdraw status," she said. WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS WIDELY PRAISE KAROLINE LEAVITT AS SHE ANNOUNCES EXIT FROM TRUMP ADMINISTRATION Zacharia was also pressed on her fumbled briefing. "What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate with very little prep time," Zacharia said. "Given the fact that I'd been on the job less than maybe eight hours and had a briefing book in the morning, I feel like I did my very best, Sean, to deliver for the American people that day." Zacharia's debut drew scrutiny over several verbal stumbles, including a moment when she mistakenly referred to her husband as "my president" before correcting herself, as well as the briefing's brevity, during which she took questions from just three journalists in 14 minutes. Karoline Leavitt’s first White House press briefing lasted nearly 47 minutes, while Sean Spicer’s debut ran roughly 79 minutes. While Sarah Huckabee Sanders’ first briefing as press secretary lasted about 23 minutes in 2017. TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY FACES FIRST MAJOR TEST AS WHITE HOUSE BRIEFING ROOM ENTERS NEW ERA A White House official told MS NOW earlier this week that she could end up with a shorter tenure than Anthony Scaramucci, whose notoriously brief stint as President Donald Trump's White House communications director lasted just 10 days before he was ousted in July 2017. "Getting behind the podium is tough, but she got off on the wrong foot," the unnamed White House official said. "She needs to get much better, fast, otherwise she'll break Scaramucci's record." Zacharia clearly did not recover enough in her short media sprint this week — where she attempted to clear up confusion about her lawyer credentials — and instead was pushed out of the job on Friday without another shot at the podium. The White House doubled down on supporting Zacharia Wednesday when asked by Fox News Digital for comment on the Scaramucci comparison reportedly coming from the White House. "Katie is a fabulous and wonderful addition to the team. She is uniquely qualified and whip smart to help inform the American people about all the great things President Trump and his Administration have been doing, and she will do an incredible job as Press Secretary," White House Communications Director Steven Cheung told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The White House X account @PressSec, formerly run by Leavitt before switching to White House Press Office, never switched over to Zacharia, and has still not posted since Oct. 7. Zacharia, whom Trump described as an attorney when announcing her appointment, previously served as senior communications adviser to Trump Media & Technology Group, which operates the president's social media platform, Truth Social. She also served earlier this year as deputy assistant secretary for public affairs and a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security for just six weeks. Fox News' Peter Doocy contributed to this report.

articles.title: Gabriel Rufián publica un libro para plantar cara a la extrema derecha con mensaje: "Cómo ganar a los fachas (Leer antes de votar)"
articles.standfirst: Saldrá a la venta el 20 de octubre justo en la previa de la campaña electoral
articles.summary: Saldrá a la venta el 20 de octubre justo en la previa de la campaña electoral
articles.body: A poco más de un mes de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, Gabriel Rufián vuelve a situarse en el centro del debate político. El portavoz de ERC y cabeza de lista al Congreso publicará el próximo 20 de octubre un libro bajo el título 'Cómo ganar a los fachas (Leer antes de votar)'. La obra llega en un momento clave para la izquierda española y con el reto de reflexionar sobre cómo frenar el avance de la extrema derecha y construir un espacio político capaz de competir de forma unitaria en las urnas. Según ha explicado la editorial Now Books, que publica el volumen junto a Abacus, el libro propone una reflexión sobre el crecimiento de la extrema derecha y plantea herramientas para hacerle frente desde posiciones progresistas. La obra incluye, según la editorial, una "disección de la extrema derecha", analiza las claves de su auge y expone alternativas para impulsar un frente común desde la izquierda. Rufián ha explicado que escribió el libro durante los últimos meses y que el proceso le sirvió para ordenar muchas de las ideas que llevaba tiempo desarrollando. Entre los fragmentos adelantados destaca una reflexión muy personal del dirigente republicano: "Yo vengo de la mierda. A mí me dijeron muchas veces que adónde creía que iba y que yo no podía. A mí nadie me esperaba aquí". La editorial destaca además el tono reconocible del político catalán, marcado por el estilo directo y contundente que suele exhibir durante sus intervenciones parlamentarias. La promoción del libro no ha pasado desapercibida. En la descripción de la obra, la editorial lanza un mensaje tan llamativo como el propio título. "Si eres facha, este libro piensa en ti. Si eres de izquierdas, este libro habla de ti. Y si no sabes lo que eres, este libro es para ti. Este libro no ofrece pureza; este libro ofrece respuestas". Un planteamiento que busca ampliar el foco más allá del electorado habitual de la izquierda y abrir el debate sobre la situación política actual. La gira de presentación arrancará el 25 de octubre en Barcelona, donde Rufián estará acompañado por la periodista Àngels Barceló en el campus Ciutadella de la Universitat Pompeu Fabra. Posteriormente, el 6 de noviembre, dará a conocer el libro en Madrid junto a la comunicadora Sarah Santaolalla en el Auditorio de UGT.

articles.title: Katie Zacharia is out as White House press secretary after just 5 days on the job
articles.summary: Katie Zacharia is out as White House press secretary after just five days on the job, a senior administration official, an administration official and a source familiar with the decision said, following a widely panned first press briefing and the revelation that she represented herself as a lawyer but did not pass her bar exam. Earlier Friday, President Donald Trump said he would let Zacharia decide whether to remain as his press secretary after he suggested she was treated harshly by the media during her first week on the job.
articles.body: Katie Zacharia is out as White House press secretary after just five days on the job, a senior administration official, an administration official and a source familiar with the decision said, following a widely panned first press briefing and the revelation that she represented herself as a lawyer but did not pass her bar exam. Earlier Friday, President Donald Trump said he would let Zacharia decide whether to remain as his press secretary after he suggested she was treated harshly by the media during her first week on the job. “She’s been treated, I would say pretty nastily, and I said to Katie just two minutes ago, I said, Katie, you know, you don’t have to do this if you don’t want,” Trump said. Asked if he would keep her on the job, the president said, “I’m going to let her make that decision.” Zacharia held a brief press briefing on Tuesday, just one day after she started the job, and came under scrutiny after she had represented herself as a lawyer but acknowledged this week that she did not pass her bar exam following law school. Zacharia’s first White House press briefing lasted less than 15 minutes, during which she took only a few questions from reporters and couldn’t answer one about whether the U.S. had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine. During the briefing, Zacharia announced that Trump had asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as U.S. ambassador to Greece, sharing that information after a journalist asked whether the president was planning to fire Guilfoyle over misconduct allegations, which she has denied. Guilfoyle announced she was stepping down within hours. Zacharia had succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who left the White House position at the end of August after serving in the role since the beginning of Trump’s term in January 2025. Zacharia made a name for herself as a conservative commentator before her extraordinarily brief stint at the White House. She served as a senior communications adviser for Trump Media & Technology Group, which runs Trump’s Truth Social website. Zacharia’s time at the White House was even shorter than Anthony Scaramucci’s as White House communications director during Trump’s first term. Scaramucci served in the role for only 11 days, and his name became a descriptor for public officials whose terms were exceedingly brief. Earlier this week, the nonpartisan watchdog group Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the State Bar of California requesting an investigation into whether Zacharia broke the law by calling herself a lawyer even though she is unlicensed. Zacharia was asked Monday about what bar exam she had taken as she and the president stopped on the South Lawn to speak with reporters before boarding. Her answer was difficult to hear over the whir of Marine One’s helicopter blades, but part of Zacharia’s response included “when I moved to China.” A senior administration official confirmed Thursday that Zacharia didn’t pass the California bar exam, which was first reported by the Wall Street Journal. Zacharia told right-wing activist Jack Posobiec in an interview Thursday that she had not passed the bar exam. There is no evidence that she is licensed to practice law in any state, according to a review by NBC News. Zacharia graduated from Pepperdine Law and has said she practiced law in China. Legal experts told NBC News that only Chinese citizens can sit for the Chinese bar exam. Zacharia could have consulted on cross-border legal issues, one expert told NBC News.

articles.title: Katie Zacharia out as White House press secretary after first week
articles.summary: Katie Zacharia, President Trump's new White House press secretary, is being moved out of the role after her first week on the job, two U.S. officials told CB...
articles.body:
Washington — Katie Zacharia, President Trump's new White House press secretary, is being removed from the role after her first week on the job, two U.S. officials told CBS News on Friday.

Some White House staff learned about the change from news coverage. The New York Times first reported that she had been fired.

One aide said Zacharia spent the week unusually isolated and didn't function as a press secretary.

"No one thought she was sticking around long enough to even involve her in actual decision-making," the aide said.

Leaving the White House on Friday, the president signaled that Zacharia might not be in the role for long, saying he told her he would "reconsider" taking the job if he were in her shoes.

"They've been so nasty to her," Mr. Trump said, referring to the press. "I said, to her, 'Honestly if I were you, I'd reconsider. You think about it. But I would reconsider. You got a beautiful husband and family.' I met the family yesterday. Beautiful kids. It's like from a picture postcard. I said, 'You should reconsider. Because you don't want to go through this.'"

The abrupt shift came one week to the day since Mr. Trump announced Zacharia as his pick to replace Karoline Leavitt, who stepped aside in August. Zacharia's qualifications and background quickly came under scrutiny as questions arose over her resumé.

CBS News and other outlets reported that Zacharia has represented herself as a lawyer over the years. She graduated from Pepperdine Law School but failed the California bar exam in 2011, a fact she acknowledged on Thursday. She told the New York Times that the president of Pepperdine University advised her at one point that she could call herself a "lawyer" but not an "attorney."

Zacharia told conservative commentator Jack Posobiec that she never described herself as an "attorney at law," and said there's a "lot of misinformation around the fact that I labeled myself a lawyer."

"I was very careful how I executed this. I never came across as someone who was an attorney at law," Zacharia said.

The about-face on Zacharia's role was reminiscent of the tenure of Anthony Scaramucci, who survived just 11 days as White House communications director during Mr. Trump's first term.

"Records are made to be broken," Scaramucci said in a post on X. "But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."

articles.body:
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed mocked Vice President Vance’s recent visit to Michigan, calling it “a cute little rally.”

“JD Vance was just in Michigan. He had a cute little rally in Monroe,” El-Sayed said during an event . “He invited the like, I don’t know, five people who like him.”

Vance visited Monroe, Mich., to rally support for former Rep. Mike Rogers (R), who is facing El-Sayed in a competitive Senate race to replace retiring Sen. Gary Peters (D).

During the campaign rally, Vance attacked El-Sayed and said Michigan deserves a better candidate, a video clip posted by the New York Post shows.

“You deserve better than a little weasel who should shut his mouth and show a little gratitude to the country that gave him everything,” Vance said, addressing the crowd. “You deserve a senator who is grateful to this country.”

The Michigan Democrat responded to Vance’s “little weasel” remark by saying, “What you’re talking about is a f—ing wolverine.”

In his speech, El-Sayed mentioned that Vance wanted to raise questions about his commitment to America and said he “got a front-row seat to what my life might have been had I not been born in America. So don’t lecture me about America. I know America.”

“Let me tell you, nobody understands how deep and profound the gift of this country is like a kid who was born here but for the accident of history that allowed that to happen,” the Democratic candidate continued.

The rally comes a little more than two weeks ahead of the November midterm elections, as Republicans fight to maintain control of Congress.

While Vance rallied to show support for Rogers, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) is joining El-Sayed for the second day of a multicity campaigning effort throughout Michigan.

articles.title: Scaramucci on Zacharia’s reported firing: ‘Records are made to be broken’
articles.summary: Anthony Scaramucci weighed in on Katie Zacharia’s departure as White House press secretary Friday, noting her tenure was less than his as communications director at just five days in the role. “Records are made to be broken,” he wrote on social platform X. “But I take no pleasure in other people’s pain.” Scaramucci famously served…
articles.body:
Anthony Scaramucci weighed in on Katie Zacharia’s departure as White House press secretary Friday, noting her tenure was less than his as communications director at just five days in the role.

“Records are made to be broken,” he wrote on social platform X . “But I take no pleasure in other people’s pain.”

Scaramucci famously served just 11 days as President Trump’s White House communications director during the president’s first term.

Social media users have joked in recent days about whether Zacharia would last “one Scaramucci” after her first press briefing Tuesday was heavily scrutinized . Bets were also being taken on the prediction market site Kalshi over when she would depart the role.

“The clock is running. Thus far 1/11th of a Scaramucci,” the ex-Trump official wrote online earlier this week .

A White House official confirmed to The Hill that Zacharia is “transitioning out” of the role as the president’s top spokesperson.

She was appointed just last week to step into the role, after Karoline Leavitt left the position earlier this year. At her first briefing, Zacharia spoke for 14 minutes and took questions from only three members of the media.

Trump signaled her departure in remarks to reporters Friday before departing the White House for Georgia.

“I said, ‘Honestly, if I were you, I’d reconsider,’” the president said, referring to a conversation he said he had with Zacharia earlier.

“I said, ‘You think about it, but I would reconsider,’” he continued.

Zacharia had also been making headlines over her legal history . In the past she has identified herself as a lawyer on TV, but a report found that she was not licensed to practice law in any state, including California where she resides.

When asked about where she took the bar exam from reporters earlier this week, she said, “when I moved to China.”

The Wall Street Journal reported later that evening that Zacharia had failed the bar exam .

On subsequent news interviews, she failed to clear the issue up.

Zacharia told conservative news outlet Real America’s Voice that she “misheard” the question about where she took the bar exam, adding later that the test’s results were “inconsequential.”

articles.body: Michele Tafoya, the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota and a former broadcaster, aggressively sought to put her opponent, Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, on the defensive during a debate Friday afternoon over the billion-dollar fraud schemes that drew national attention to the state earlier this year. We have test scores down. We have crime spiking. We have a massive surplus turned into a deficit," Tafoya said. TAFOYA MAKES 'COMMON SENSE' PITCH TO DISAFFECTED DEMOCRATS AS SHE VOWS TO FIGHT MINNESOTA’S ‘SOCIALIST LURCH’ "This election is about Peggy Flanagan." Local and federal investigators have uncovered myriad fraud schemes involving daycare centers, food programs, health clinics and other operations accused of defrauding the state of up to $9 billion. Investigators say fraudsters either inflated the number of people they allegedly helped or fabricated their services altogether — all while receiving government dollars. When the issue resurfaced later in the debate, the moderator asked Flanagan directly whether, in her view, she had "any ownership over the fraud." Flanagan sought to distance herself from the issue, pointing to Walz's acknowledgment that responsibility for oversight rested with him. "The governor has been very clear that the buck stops with him," Flanagan said. "He was the one who had oversight here. I've led on issues like paid family and medical leave, nation-leading child tax credit, making sure that kids get breakfast and lunch at school. Those are the things and those are the areas where I took the lead." When Flanagan then redirected the conversation to criticism of President Donald Trump, Tafoya went on the attack. DAVID MARCUS: PEGGY FLANAGAN'S DEI RECORD AND FRAUD SCANDAL PUT MINNESOTA SENATE RACE IN THE SPOTLIGHT "Peggy, Donald Trump isn't on the ballot. You and I are on the ballot, and only one of us let $9 billion walk out the door to fraud to suggest that we that she somehow is going to be a fraud czar all of a sudden," Tafoya said. "My goodness, she was second in charge in this state, and she's just going to point her finger at Gov. Tim Walz when she demanded to be in the room where everything happened. But, suddenly, she has nothing to do with this. Again, sell it to someone else," she added. Flanagan has served as Minnesota's lieutenant governor for nearly eight years, taking office in 2019. By the time Walz announced that he would not run for re-election as governor amid political scrutiny for the fraud, Flanagan had already announced her bid for U.S. Senate. Responding to Tafoya, Flanagan doubled down on her criticism of Trump, noting that the president had recently endorsed Tafoya. "Donald Trump doesn't just endorse anybody. In fact, he endorses against people in his own party if they dare to take him on. Michele Tafoya passed his litmus test with flying colors," Flanagan said. Tafoya then laid out her own proposals for combating fraud, including tougher consequences for noncitizens who defraud Americans. "No. 1, if you're a guest of this country, and you defraud Americans, you must leave. You must leave, and you should have no pathway back," she said. FRAUD EXPERT EXPOSES HOW HIDDEN NETWORKS DROVE MINNESOTA FRAUD, OTHER MAJOR SCAMS: 'CRIMINAL ENTERPRISE' SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER "No. 2, if you're an American and you defraud your fellow Americans, we should be talking about mandatory prison minimums. Tough sentences, not an easygoing slap on the wrist. "And No. 3, if you're a state like Minnesota who cannot keep your financial house in order, why would the federal government release billions and billions of dollars to you, only to see it go to fraud?" articles.title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia fired after five days on the job
articles.summary: Trump advised Katie Zacharia to reconsider her press secretary role due to media backlash over her credentials.
articles.body:
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is “transitioning out” of her role just one week after United States President Donald Trump tapped her for the job, Al Jazeera has confirmed.

Fox News on Friday reported that Trump said there was no rush to hire Zacharia’s replacement.

Earlier Friday, Trump told reporters he told Zacharia to “reconsider” staying in the job.

“I don’t think Katie should be made to suffer like she’s suffering at the hands of the press,” Trump said as he departed the White House. “I said to her, ‘Honestly, if I were you, I’d reconsider. You think about it.’”

Zacharia said she had received a call about the role last week. She succeeded Karoline Leavitt.

Trump later announced her appointment and described her as “an attorney”. However, over the last week, the question of whether Zacharia, a graduate of California’s Pepperdine University law school, had actually passed the bar exam to work as an attorney came under fire.

In an interview, she told Fox News on Thursday that she did not pass the bar exam.

She lasted five days on the job, half the length of Anthony Scaramucci’s tenure as director of communications, who served for 10 days during Trump’s first administration.

Al Jazeera correspondent Kimberly Halkett explained that the appointment and subsequent reversal could create further problems for Trump as Republicans prepare for a pivotal midterm election.

“The fact that there was that major credibility issue as well as a shaky performance is what sealed her fate,” said Halkett. “This makes the president look impulsive at a time when he’s already being criticised for not having a campaign that is really on track to win in November.”
